title: Set the system-wide locale on Arch Linux
summary: Change the default language and region settings for the entire system. This affects how dates, numbers, and messages are displayed for all users unless overridden.
prerequisites: The desired locale must already be generated (see 'Generate a new locale on Arch Linux').

steps.explain: Use the localectl command to set the LANG variable system-wide. Replace <LOCALE_ID> with the exact identifier from the first column of your uncommented entry in /etc/locale.gen (e.g., en_US.UTF-8).

rollback.explain: Set the locale back to the previous value (usually en_US.UTF-8).
rollback.gui: Edit /etc/locale.conf as root and change the LANG line back to the previous value.

warnings: Changes take effect for new sessions. You may need to log out and back in.
Desktop environments like GNOME or KDE may override this setting in their own settings.
